A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SUFT research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, appendices, and checklists are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original Atari and MuJoCo training experiments, including per-environment rewards, significance tests, learning curves, and ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds an inertia-regularizer comparison, synthetic inequality tests, and Atari diagnostics of the bound.

M1.justification: Both versions store behavior-policy value outputs and add the same weighted SUFT discrepancy term to the value-network loss. The new DQN and PPO pseudocode documents the existing procedure; it does not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: V2 adds standard-normal synthetic inputs for testing the loss inequality in Appendix D.4. Both versions retain all 57 Atari games and five MuJoCo environments; changes in the number of valid games concern metric eligibility, not removal of evaluated environments.

E2.justification: Section 5.5 and Table 11 add Double DQN with an inertia regularizer as a comparator against baseline and SUFT Double DQN. The existing DQN variants, PPO, SAC, and buffer-size comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: V2 raises the numerator/denominator eligibility threshold for reward summaries from greater than zero to greater than one, materially changing the aggregate evaluation. It also introduces a billion-sample Gaussian test and Atari diagnostics using Bellman approximations. Appendix D.2 separately reports an L1 PPO coefficient of 2.5, whereas v1 stated 5 for Atari PPO generally; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds three substantive analyses: causal-bound optimization versus inertia regularization, empirical validity of the L2 inequality, and the magnitude of the delta term relative to training losses. The original coefficient sweep, overhead analysis, and buffer/agent ablation remain; v1 Table 5 is relocated to v2 Table 1.

E5.justification: The retained experiments use the same ten random-seed runs, upper-middle median convention, two-sided t-tests, and learning-curve bands showing the 10th and 90th percentiles. V2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Retained per-environment rewards and p-values are unchanged, but revised aggregation changes DQN's mean ratio from 2427.06% to 383.19% and the small-buffer comparison from 503.36% to 437.05%. New results include the inertia comparator's 83.21% ratio, approximately 82% and 79% inequality-satisfaction rates, and delta-magnitude curves. The revised PPO sweep also reverses the ranking of coefficients 5 and 10. These aggregate changes do not demonstrate deteriorating learned performance.

T1.justification: The causal-bound assumptions, definitions, binary and multiple-treatment theorems, and proofs are retained. V2's equations 17 and 18 specialize existing inequalities for empirical checks; they provide no new theoretical guarantee for L2 loss.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction substantially narrow the headline reward-ratio claim from up to 2427% to up to 383%. The introduction also reduces the larger-buffer comparison from 503.36% to 437.05%. The factual-loss-bound contribution and claimed 96% buffer reduction remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive mechanism interpretations: the inertia comparison is presented as evidence for causal-bound optimization rather than generic regularization, frequent empirical inequality satisfaction is offered to explain L2 performance, and the estimated delta magnitude is argued not to meaningfully loosen the bound. V1 acknowledged the L2 limitation but lacked these supporting interpretations.

D1.justification: V2 adds explicit DQN/PPO pseudocode, explains reuse of PPO rollout values, and supplies a code-access URL where v1 only described supplementary code. The new diagnostics disclose sampling and approximation details. Existing hardware, overhead measurements, library defaults, and main training budgets remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Mnih et al.'s 2013 Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning reference to support the DQN pseudocode. The previous references and the related-work positioning around causal reinforcement learning and factual-loss bounds are retained.

P1.justification: V2 expands selected introductory explanations, adds a pseudocode appendix, and promotes the existing ablation discussion into Section 5.4. Experimental material moves from Appendix C to D, and the publication footer is updated. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the delta diagnostic figure, inertia-comparison table, and algorithm displays, and relocates the existing ablation table. Reward-summary plots and captions reflect revised eligible games, Figure 2 is rescaled, and Figure 4 is resized and redrawn. Retained learning-curve images and principal table formats remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency through explicit pseudocode, a code-access pointer, and targeted diagnostics. Its stricter ratio rule addresses near-random-baseline inflation and produces more restrained headline claims. These gains are limited: the approximate diagnostics do not resolve the L2 guarantee gap or uniquely establish a causal mechanism. The revised PPO sweep also ranks coefficient 10 above 5, while Appendix D.2 still calls 5 best.
